## Natural history notes

A medium-sized ponerine ant characterized by a slender dark body with a subtle silvery sheen, long legs, and a narrow waist that gives it a wasp-like appearance. In Florida, the Common Silvery Hunter Ant is found mainly in warm humid habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, leaf litter, rotting wood, logs, and shaded yards, especially in southern parts of the state. Colonies are small and workers are active predators, hunting tiny insects and other arthropods in litter and wood cavities while also scavenging, making them part of the hidden ground-layer predator community.
